<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5e1342a6e07b287e0b829332ac565872f568666f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d937ded5d5f41b036e4ae14b521762e6d643a3b4` — the merge of head `c053f4cabaa4929a80aabba4320f406846a74d12` into base `5e1342a6e07b287e0b829332ac565872f568666f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d937ded5d5f41b036e4ae14b521762e6d643a3b4 && git checkout d937ded5d5f41b036e4ae14b521762e6d643a3b4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5e1342a6e07b287e0b829332ac565872f568666f c053f4cabaa4929a80aabba4320f406846a74d12 && git checkout -B drift-repro 5e1342a6e07b287e0b829332ac565872f568666f && git merge --no-ff c053f4cabaa4929a80aabba4320f406846a74d12

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5e1342a6e07b287e0b829332ac565872f568666f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c053f4cabaa4929a80aabba4320f406846a74d12`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-analytics/src/measure-currency-coherence.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/__tests__/record-currency-analytics.test.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/__tests__/currency-mode-relay.test.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/__tests__/query-dataset.test.ts, .changeset/27579-fixed-currency-measure-guards.md + packages/services/service-analytics/src/analytics-service.ts (`compile`, `registerDataset`, `queryDataset`, `enrichResultColumns` currency chain), packages/services/service-analytics/src/plugin.ts (`sourceFieldMeta` relay), packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-compiler.ts:860, packages/spec/src/ui/dataset.zod.ts (`DatasetMeasureSchema`, `DerivedMeasureOp`), PR #27338 `fea128ce` / `80b98fb8` / `507ed8f9`

Face: narrowing (`record-recognisers --paths` returns no `hits`; the changeset's `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` decides). Read: card #27579, ruling 6486427200 on #8345 (letter A), triage 6515345174, dispatch-27579.md, PR body, os-dev-report 6516665481, the 5-file diff, PR #27338 and its dropped first draft.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Shape 1 (guard 1, fixed arm)** — `field.defaultCurrency !== undefined && field.defaultCurrency !== m.currency`, aggregated measures only (`m.derived` ⇒ `field` undefined). `defaultCurrency` is relayed by `sourceFieldMeta` ONLY under `currencyMode === 'fixed'` (plugin.ts:1447), so a `dynamic` field (schema-materialised default included) cannot trip it. Exactly the ruled shape. Message names dataset, measure, declared code, field, object, the fixed code and the fix (delete `currency`; column takes the field's code). Pinned red → green at registration, `queryDataset`, `previewDrafts`.
- **Shape 2 (guard 2, fixed arm)** — `pairRefused` adds `a.fixed && b.fixed && a.code !== b.code` to the unchanged record pair. Every op (`sum`/`difference`/`ratio`/`product`, the whole `DerivedMeasureOp` enum) pinned. `fixed` is set only when the code IS the field's `fixed` code (restated or not); a derived `sum`/`difference` is `fixed` iff every operand is. Message names derived measure, op, both operands and their codes, and the fix. Exactly the ruled shape in the ruled cases.
- **Controls, all pinned and all unchanged in behaviour:** restated `fixed` code accepted (registration + both request doors, column prints `EUR`); measure `currency` over a `dynamic` field not judged; `count` operand (`count(*)`) not compared — `per_invoice`, `usd_per_invoice`, `eur_per_invoice`; `fixed` vs tenant (`usd_and_tenant`) not judged; record-mode arms — the record tests in `record-currency-analytics.test.ts` are untouched by the diff and `provablyDiffer` / the record half of `pairRefused` are byte-equivalent to `recordPairDiffers`.
- **Q2, explicit `currency` over a `dynamic` field in Shape 2** — the PR marks it `fixed: false` so `sum(tenant_as_jpy, usd)` compiles (pinned as CONTROL); `fea128ce` refused it. The ruling's Shape 2 text is "operands resolve to two different **`fixed`** codes" and it lists "a measure `currency` over a `dynamic` field … stays legal" among the not-judged. An explicit JPY over a `dynamic` field is not the field's `fixed` code under any reading of the words, so the PR follows the ruling's literal text and the dev was right not to widen. **I do not FAIL for this.** But the ruling's *reason* (Prime Directive 12, "an answer that is not a number in any currency") applies to JPY+USD exactly as to EUR+USD, and the first draft the ruling names as the starting point refused it — so the maintainer may have meant "two different known codes". **needs_decision (not blocking):** whether Shape 2 should also compare an explicit measure `currency` (over a `dynamic` field) against a `fixed` code. If yes, it is a further narrowing on its own card; this PR's CONTROL pin is the one line that would flip.
- **Q3, `fixed` propagation** — `ratio`/`product` resolve to `undefined` (`common = []`), so a derived measure built on one has no monetary operand there: no false refusal (`sum(usd_per_invoice, eur)` compiles, matching the column chain, where a derived measure carries no currency unless explicit). `sum`/`difference` propagate code + `fixed`, pinned one level up (`usd_twice` → `mixed`). No silent miss the ruling's text requires.
- **Q4, both doors** — `registerDataset` (analytics-service.ts:2588) and `queryDataset` (:2688) both call the one `compile()` → `compileDataset` → `assertMeasureCurrenciesCoherent` (dataset-compiler.ts:860); the `previewDrafts` branch (:2698) and the engine query come after. Refusal precedes any query. Pinned for both shapes × {`queryDataset`, `previewDrafts`}.
- **Q6, moved pins** — `git diff fea128ce pr-27991` on `currency-mode-relay.test.ts` and `query-dataset.test.ts` is empty: byte-identical to the draft the ruling names as the starting point. `m_explicit_fixed` JPY→EUR (restates) and the chain pin moves to a `dynamic` field: both are the exact shape the ruling now refuses, so the old pins could not stand; the dynamic-wins and tenant-ctx assertions they carried are kept. Not hiding a regression.
- **Q7, in-tree callers** — independent survey: 16 files declare `measures:`; 0 set a measure `currency` (the one textual hit is a prose example in `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/dashboards.md:299`, the owed follow-up); the only derived measures (`revenue-pulse`, `chart-gallery`) are `ratio` of two `count(*)`. 0 of either shape; dev's count confirmed.
- **Q9, dogfood** — dev reports the full battery at `c053f4ca`: 357/360 files (3 skipped), 2875 passed / 20 skipped, 0 failed, under the verify lock. Package suite 196 files / 4752 passed, red-on-base 10/83 and three ablations reported with restore. Check-runs at the head at review time: 21 success, 13 skipped, 12 in_progress (Lint & Repo Gates, Test Core 1–8, Type Check ×3), 0 failures.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/service-analytics` **minor** with a **BREAKING** paragraph — as the ruling fixes (the fixed group refuses `major` before GA). `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` on both PR body and changeset, both recognised spellings (`clause2-line.mjs`). ADR-0087 marker `<!-- adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription) … -->` matches the gate's regex and names a category ADR-0087 §750 lists. `Skills-docs: follow-up owed — …` present; seat files the card and rewrites the line to `#N`. No spec/contract key touched; `dataset-compiler.ts` untouched (file surface held). Correct.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`count` over a currency field is resolved as monetary.** `resolvedOf` never reads `m.aggregate`, so `{ aggregate: 'count', field: 'amt_usd' }` resolves to `USD, fixed` and `ratio(count(amt_usd), sum(amt_eur))` would refuse, while the ruling says "a non-monetary operand (a `count`) is not compared". The pins cover `count(*)` only. Not a must-fix: (a) the record arm on `main` has had the identical corner since #27338 (a `count` over a record amount resolves to `record`), (b) the fixed column chain on `main` (`enrichResultColumns`, `monetary = !!mc.currency || meta?.type === 'currency'`, no aggregate test) labels that very count column with the field's code, so the guard refuses what the column would print, (c) 0 in tree. Recommend one change on both seams on the owed follow-up card: gate `resolvedOf` and the fixed chain's `monetary` on `AMOUNT_AGGREGATES`, as the record chain already does.
- **Derived measure with its own `currency` over a `fixed` common code** — `{ derived: sum(eur, eur), currency: 'JPY' }` compiles: Shape 1 reads "the aggregated field's `fixed` code" and a derived measure has none, so this is outside the ruled text, but it prints EUR amounts as JPY one level up — the same wrong-label the ruling refuses at level 0 (the record arm does refuse the derived analogue). For the follow-up card, not this PR.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is glossed in `clause2-line.mjs` as "widens one surface and narrows another"; this diff only narrows. The ruling fixed the spelling, so noted, not re-ruled.
- `dataset-compiler.ts:860` comment names the record arms only (dev flagged; outside surface; incomplete, not false).
- Error messages: leak nothing beyond the dataset's own name/object/measures and the object's declared `fixed` code; no tenant, ctx or row data. Good.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing holds against the published spec on `main`: `DatasetMeasure.currency` is "Display currency code", and `enrichResultColumns` lets it win over a `fixed` field — so before this PR the spec let an author print EUR amounts labelled JPY, and `computeDerived` let USD−EUR compile to a bare number. Both refusals make the spec's own semantics real at the one compile seam, with the fix in the message, and take no capability away that produced a correct answer. The `fixed` flag on `Resolved` is the minimal carrier: the record half of guard 2 is unchanged and the fixed half is one conjunction, so the two arms cannot drift. Test design is sound: red-on-base, every op, one level up, both doors, and five controls incl. the open Q2 reading pinned as a CONTROL so a later ruling flips one visible line. The re-application from `fea128ce` is faithful where the ruling asks (moved pins identical) and deliberately departs only on the Q2 reading, which it surfaces.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-2w318c`
Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4czuTWNgKR22fKv7jia (seat subagent)`

**VERDICT: PASS**
